round: 2a (P1 PATTERN, one fallback: demux-wide) ; 2b (SOLVERSYN t5 failed its exit criterion, written fallback COMBSYN L7 x4 at the 65k cap) ; 2c COMPACTOR (FC3) ; 2d CQ1-3 (FC4)

FC1.turns: two: t1 writes Predictor (clean repeats), t2 carries the model's own t1 reply as history and is the scored turn
FC1.grader: patgen_iso (predictor in its own bwrap process, fed one digit per round trip, 60 CPU s)
FC1.scoring: per stream: accuracy rescaled (n-gram anchor = 0.2, oracle = 1; floor tier chance..oracle); 3 streams per tier; points = sum of tier weights x tier score, /100 = item score
FC1.note: v2 (6 tiers, noisy-period 20) is kept as the 2208122 history; demux-wide shows no example stream so the t2 prompt is byte-identical to the one the Claude rows answered (their replies were re-graded, not re-run)

FC2.scoring: each instance = 5 targets (groups T1-T5), score = share of groups passed; item = mean of the 4 instances; a reply cut at the stated 65,536-token cap (reasoning included) scores 0 (meta.hard_item_cap, applied by the runner as for patgen)
FC2.note: limit = certified minimum (7) on every target, so a lazy or size-<=6 answer scores 0; the answer is a literal dict of terms (no code is run for the model's search)

FC3.family: compactor2 (interactive console, one command per reply)
FC3.scoring: floor 15 + climb 25 + edge 25+35*efficiency(stop turn 30..90) - 4 per fault; /100
FC3.engine: simulator + Session loop ported (crucibleforge/gen/compactor2.py, probe-c/p1c2.py); not an engine family (no materialize): the interactive runner hookup is task 7

FC4.family: classic-code CQ1-3 (4.1 text, byte for byte)
FC4.rows: stored 4.1 rows re-scored; no new runs
FC4.scoring: source rule = one group (a violation fails that group only); truncated rows dropped (not scored 0)
FC4.interpreter: python 3.13 (the stored rows' grading interpreter; 3.14 changes ',' grouping of fractional digits)
FC4.rescore: docs/fc4-rescore/ (script, rows, aggregate); scoring transform = crucibleforge/cq_rule_group.py

nominal_answer_tokens.note: patgen LEVELS answer_tokens 900 per turn; real replies 10-40k with thinking, reported not capped
